messages.text: Alpine condemn online abuse since Colapinto crash, Norris remarks

metadata.summary: Alpine have condemned the online abuse and hate aimed at drivers and others in Formula 1 since the incident in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that saw Franco Colapinto cause a three-car collision with Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris.
metadata.content: Alpine condemn online abuse since Franco Colapinto three-car Azerbaijan GP crash with Pierre Gasly, Lando Norris | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Update Alpine condemn online abuse since Franco Colapinto three-car Azerbaijan GP crash with Pierre Gasly, Lando Norris Franco Colapinto's mistake at first Safety Car restart in Baku led to chain-reaction accident that also saw team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris drop out; Alpine condemn social media abuse aimed at all sides seen since crash Sunday 27 September 2026 14:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix Alpine have condemned the online abuse and hate aimed at drivers and others in Formula 1 since the incident in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that saw Franco Colapinto cause a three-car collision with Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris. Alpine driver Colapinto triggered the accident in the Baku race's first Safety Car restart when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of team-mate Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside. "Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport," Alpine said as part of a statement issued on Sunday. metadata.summary: Brandt Snedeker has given a self-critical assessment of his own Presidents Cup captaincy so far, with time quickly running out to avoid an embarrassing defeat for Team USA on home soil.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: Brandt Snedeker reveals captaincy criticisms ahead of singles as Team USA look to avoid Medinah upset | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: Brandt Snedeker reveals captaincy criticisms ahead of singles as Team USA look to avoid Medinah upset Can Team USA avoid a shock home defeat at the Presidents Cup? How the International Team are closing on history but have a big final day ahead at Medinah; watch the Sunday singles live from 4.30pm on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 27 September 2026 07:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the third day of the 2026 Presidents Cup, where the International Team moved closer to a famous win on American soil Brandt Snedeker has given a self-critical assessment of his own Presidents Cup captaincy so far, with time quickly running out to avoid an embarrassing defeat for Team USA on home soil. Team USA came into the week as overwhelming favourites to claim a record-extending 11th consecutive victory, in a biennial event where much of the pre-tournament narrative was around whether change was needed to make it more competitive. Next to no hope had been given to Geoff Ogilvy's International Team, who earned their only Presidents Cup win in 1998 and have lost every edition since a 17-17 tie in 2003, but they are now five points away from completing a seismic shock at Medinah. messages.text: Is Russell really back after Baku brilliance?

metadata.summary: George Russell produced the most statistically complete weekend of his Formula 1 career to win the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, but did the performance confirm the Brit is back to his best?
metadata.content: George Russell: Is Mercedes driver really back after 'Grand Slam' Azerbaijan GP win cut Kimi Antonelli's F1 title lead? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis George Russell: Is Mercedes driver really back after 'Grand Slam' Azerbaijan GP win cut Kimi Antonelli's F1 title lead? George Russell drove superbly to win the Azerbaijan Grand Prix; Russell reduced his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead to 66 points; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix Sunday 27 September 2026 09:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Azerbaijan GP saw a dramatic ending as Valtteri Bottas crashed on the final lap as George Russell just beat Max Verstappen to victory by one tenth of a second. George Russell produced the most statistically complete weekend of his Formula 1 career to win the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, but did the performance confirm the Brit is back to his best? Russell drove superbly in Baku to claim the first Grand Slam of his career, taking pole position, leading from lights-to-flag on his way to victory, and setting the fastest lap of the race. The result saw Russell reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's lead at the top of the world championship to 66 points with eight rounds remaining, ensuring some intrigue remains as the season enters its closing stretch.
